bug_semantics: A one-character tcpprep include/exclude specification is duplicated into a two-byte heap buffer (mode byte plus NUL). parse_xX_str recognizes the mode and unconditionally advances the pointer by two bytes before calling parse_cidr; that pointer is one byte past the allocation. parse_cidr then calls mask_cidr6, whose initial **cidrin test reads the invalid address, producing the reported heap-buffer-overflow read through doOptInclude -> parse_xX_str -> parse_cidr -> mask_cidr6.
flaw_origin: Commit 3941c24fbcdf2a9822df5d2a84ac0c3f5612e408 introduced -x/-X parsing and first wrote the causal pattern in tcpreplay.c: each recognized selector advanced str by two and parsed the result without first proving that a delimiter and payload existed. Commit 90c47b79caa0b7685e6d0d737e01b786ac4ac475 later extracted the same logic into xX.c, and a9a5ec78124ea11c0ab9e1a8a0d74ce6616c4790 exposed that shared parser to tcpprep; those are propagation/attack-path commits, not the first writer of the flaw.
ai_marker: absent; the raw BIC commit object names human author and committer Aaron Turner <synfinatic@gmail.com>, and its message has no Co-Authored-By, Generated-with, AI-tool trailer, or bot identity.
evidence: First-party reports https://github.com/appneta/tcpreplay/issues/958 and /issues/959 reproduce the two-byte allocation and out-of-bounds read at src/common/cidr.c:mask_cidr6 through doOptInclude and parse_xX_str on 4.5.1 build 6fcbf0324088561d95c356fe8337f4faac275f1a; maintainer comments identify a duplicate fixed for 4.5.2. Original report https://github.com/appneta/tcpreplay/issues/928 identifies the unchecked str + 2 operation, and PR https://github.com/appneta/tcpreplay/pull/951.patch is a one-commit patch whose From SHA is 697d9ed51b8b439de14ac3baf98b1331ed2be51c. In the validated clone, git log -L :parse_xX_str:src/common/xX.c leads through extraction commit 90c47b79caa0b7685e6d0d737e01b786ac4ac475; git log -S 'str = str + 2' -- tcpreplay.c xX.c src/common/xX.c and git show 3941c24fbcdf2a9822df5d2a84ac0c3f5612e408 show that 3941c24fbcdf2a9822df5d2a84ac0c3f5612e408 first added the unchecked advances and parse_cidr calls. git show of its immediate parent 9cdc7d3ef38da6b7cce767a1913544dcdc2acb8a plus git grep for 'str = str + 2' confirm that the vulnerable parser block/advance is absent there. Commit 18f9a1d9184167ce77e41571911e90d763e816f3 later added mask_cidr6 and its leading dereference, explaining the reported crash site without superseding the unchecked caller as root cause. Fix commit 697d9ed51b8b439de14ac3baf98b1331ed2be51c adds an early str[0] && str[1] == 0 syntax-error guard before the switch. Tag commits are v4.5.1=0ba7d17fcb9ddedf61168f99c249b30731310d4e, v4.5.2-beta1=0b0e72850228093c0864f270ea532da0f29498c6, and v4.5.2=98169912173986cc48a4ad325997dcc20c38af28. git merge-base --is-ancestor confirms the BIC is in v4.5.1, the fix is absent from v4.5.1, and the fix is in both v4.5.2-beta1 and v4.5.2.
reasoning: The advisory's immediate fault is not allocation in our_safe_strdup: that function correctly allocates the one-character input plus terminator. The causal mistake is accepting that one-character selector as structurally complete and moving two bytes before parsing. History shows the same unchecked operation originated in the 2002 -x/-X feature, was later copied/extracted into the shared parse_xX_str helper, and then became reachable from tcpprep; selecting the extraction, tcpprep adoption, IPv6 helper, reported release merge, or fix would mistake propagation or manifestation for first introduction. The immediate parent directly lacks the parser block, while the BIC is an ancestor of the vulnerable 4.5.1 boundary. The atomic PR commit fixes the same causal condition before pointer advancement and is included at the maintainer-stated 4.5.2 boundary. Finally, the BIC's raw commit object contains only Aaron Turner's human author/committer identities and an ordinary feature message, with no commit-object AI attribution, so the BIC-only verdict is NOT_AI.
